description: Single-panel engineering stress–strain plot (mechanical property curve) for ferritic low-density steels. The x-axis is "Engineering strain (%)", 0–50 with ticks every 10; the y-axis is "Engineering stress (MPa)", 0–800 with ticks/gridlines every 200. Four tensile curves are drawn, each labelled in the same colour as the curve: magenta "9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti", blue "8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti", red "6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti", and black "IF". The magenta curve (highest Al and highest C) is the strongest: it shows a low-strain step/plateau just below the 600 MPa gridline, rises to a peak slightly above the 600 MPa line at roughly 10–12% strain, then drops in a near-vertical segment at about 12–13% strain. A black arrow annotated "Discontinuous yielding" points at the low-strain part of this magenta curve. The blue curve peaks between the 400 and 600 MPa gridlines and ends in an abrupt near-vertical drop at ~16–17% strain. The red curve rises to a plateau between the 400 and 600 MPa gridlines extending to ~31–33% strain before a sharp drop, and the black IF curve is the weakest (plateau near 300 MPa) but the most ductile, reaching ~48% strain. No numeric peak values are printed; all positions are read against the 200 MPa / 10% gridlines.

observations.observation: The plot axes are engineering stress (MPa) from 0 to 800 with 200 MPa ticks, versus engineering strain (%) from 0 to 50 with 10% ticks.
Four curves are labelled directly on the plot, each in the colour of its curve: magenta '9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti', blue '8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti', red '6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti' and black 'IF'.

A black annotation reading 'Discontinuous yielding' with an arrow points to the low-strain portion of the magenta 9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti curve, which is the curve with the highest carbon content (0.04C) labelled on the plot.

The magenta curve peaks slightly above the 600 MPa gridline at approximately 10-12% strain and then falls in a near-vertical segment at about 12-13% strain, giving it the lowest strain at final load drop of the four curves.
The blue 8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti curve rises to a peak between the 400 and 600 MPa gridlines and ends in an abrupt near-vertical load drop at roughly 16-17% strain.
The red 6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti curve reaches a broad plateau between the 400 and 600 MPa gridlines that extends to about 31-33% strain before a sharp drop.
The black curve labelled 'IF' shows the lowest flow stress, with a plateau near the 300 MPa level, but the largest elongation, extending to roughly 48% strain before dropping at the end of the test.
Ranking by flow stress, IF < 6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti < 8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti < 9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti; ranking by elongation to fracture is the reverse.
The figure is a single panel with no numeric data labels; stress and strain values can only be read relative to the 200 MPa and 10% gridlines.

The caption states the tensile curves show discontinuous yielding as a result of the presence of free C in the matrix, in contrast to continuous yielding in high Al-containing and conventional 'interstitial free' alloys.
The caption attributes the figure to reference 20 (superscript 20), i.e. the curves are reproduced from a prior study.

The citing text states that the presence of free C in ferritic steels can cause discontinuous yielding in the tensile curve (Fig. 10), which can give rise to surface stretcher marks on sheets after forming, and that carbon should preferably be stabilized.
The citing text states that Al content in ferritic steels needs to be below 6.5 wt.%, which is a claim outside the plotted data range (the curves shown are for 6.8, 8.1 and 9.7 Al alloys).

subfigures.description: Engineering stress (MPa, 0–800) versus engineering strain (%, 0–50) plot with four labelled tensile curves: magenta 9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti (with a black arrow annotated 'Discontinuous yielding' pointing to its low-strain region), blue 8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti, red 6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti, and black IF. Strength increases in the order IF < 6.8Al < 8.1Al < 9.7Al, while elongation to the final load drop decreases in the same order.

unreadable_items: No numeric values are printed on the plot (no data labels, no tabulated values); peak stresses and elongations can only be estimated against the 200 MPa / 10% gridlines
The exact shape of the magenta curve's initial yield step at very low strain (<2%) is compressed against the y-axis and cannot be read precisely
